subject: Where are our audit artefacts? Export options & retention Q&A
messages:
From: Diane Park <diane.park@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: secops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exporting audit & access logs: retention + delivery options

Hi Vanessa —

We’re working through an internal compliance questionnaire and need a clear description of our options for getting audit and access logs out of Redwood. Specifically:

- What are the default retention windows for: (1) audit logs (configuration changes, admin actions) and (2) access logs (API request/response metadata, IPs)?
- Can we request a point-in-time snapshot export (e.g., preserve the last 180 days) and what format will that be in?
- Do you support push exports to our S3 (bucket + prefix)? Is that synchronous (near-real-time) or a scheduled/export job?
- For deletion requests (user or org data removal), how are audit/access records handled? Soft-delete vs physical deletion?
- Typical lead time and cost if we ask Redwood to produce a bulk historical export beyond default retention?

We need these in writing for our auditors. Appreciate a short matrix or bullets so I can paste into our questionnaire.

Thanks,
Diane Park
Director, Compliance
Acme Health

[Attachment: compliance-questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Diane Park <diane.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: secops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exporting audit & access logs: retention + delivery options

Hi Diane — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Q&A you can share with your auditors; I’ve also attached a short export-instructions PDF and can schedule a quick run-through if helpful.

Summary (short matrix):
- Default retention (hosted): audit logs = 90 days; access logs = 90 days.
- Dedicated / Private customers: configurable retention up to 7 years depending on contract and storage tier.
- Snapshot export: yes — point-in-time exports available for up to the retained window. Exports delivered as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or CSV; syslog (RFC5424) streaming available for access logs.
- Push to customer S3: supported — can do scheduled pushes (hourly/daily) or on-demand exports to your bucket (S3 path + role-based write).
- Deletion semantics: user/data deletion requests remove customer data payloads; audit metadata (who changed what and when) is treated as part of the audit trail and can be retained per policy unless a specific legal e-discovery order requires redaction; physical deletion of audit records is possible for Private/Dedicated with a retention contract but hosted defaults follow 90-day expiration before permanent purge.
- Bulk historical export (> retention): for backfill beyond hosted retention we run an assisted export job. Typical lead time: 3–7 business days depending on volume; if export requires deep cold retrieval or manual processing it can take up to 14 days. Export fees may apply for large-volume backfills.

Technical notes (fields included in exports): timestamp, event_type, actor_id (internal user id), actor_email (if available), target_resource, change_summary (text), request_id, ip_address, user_agent, region, model/version (if applicable).

If this covers it, I’ll mark this as the official response. If you want a formal statement we can push to your security mailbox as a PDF and include SLA language for Dedicated.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

[Attachment: audit-export-instructions.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 14:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exporting audit & access logs: retention + delivery options

Vanessa — quick confirmations and recommended wording for Acme:

- Hosted defaults: audit logs = 90 days; access logs = 90 days. We do not automatically retain access logs for 365 days on hosted tiers. Extended retention is offered via Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private deployments where retention can be configured up to 7 years depending on storage class.

- Snapshot vs backfill: point-in-time snapshot exports are available for any data that still exists within the retention window (i.e., you can take a snapshot of the last 180 days only if those 180 days are still retained). For historical data outside retention, we offer an assisted backfill export (we rehydrate from any cold stores where applicable). Typical turnaround:
  * On-demand snapshot (within retention): 24–48 hours to prepare and upload to customer S3 (depending on size).
  * Assisted backfill (> retention): 3–10 business days for mid-size volumes (<= 10 TB); up to 14 business days for very large volumes or when manual reconciliation is needed.
  * If cold retrieval from long-term archive is required, add up to 7 days for retrieval.

- Export formats: NDJSON (preferred), CSV (flattened), syslog RFC5424 (streaming). Exports include the fields Vanessa listed; sensitive payloads (customer-provided PII in request bodies) are excluded from audit payloads unless explicitly requested and approved for compliance reasons.

- IP addresses / user_agent: included by default for access logs. No tenant-level toggle required — functionally visible in exports and live syslog.

- Deletion semantics: hosted pipeline runs automated purge jobs post-retention window. For Dedicated/Private customers we can run a targeted purge job that physically deletes records and returns a receipts summary. For hosted environments, we separate logical deletion (making data inaccessible) from permanent purge; auditors usually accept the retention + purge schedule along with the export receipts.

- Costs: small exports (<100 GB) generally included as part of support; mid (100 GB–5 TB) handled via standard export fee schedule; large backfills (>5 TB) require a quote (engineering time + egress/storage). I recommend we include a short fee band matrix in the response. Marissa — can you draft the fee bands and I’ll add the technical caveats.

Attaching a tiny sample syslog export and a short checklist for S3 permissions to share with the customer.
